CHIEF COMPLAINT
Followup of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bruce is a 60-year-old male with past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension presenting for followup of his chronic conditions. Patient reports it has been a crazy year and a half with anxiety and pressure related to holiday preparations. He did have a nice holiday seeing family after about two years, though it was stressful and required a lot of work. He is planning to take a vacation somewhere warm in the new year.

Regarding depression, patient reports that over the summer he started going for long walks outside every morning, which he enjoyed due to nice weather and plants in full bloom. This also encouraged weekend yard work and physical activity with sun exposure. However, with seasonal changes and cold weather, he has not been able to continue this routine and is looking for alternative strategies. Patient denies suicidal or homicidal ideation. He is not ready to try medications at this time and is interested in exploring alternative options including therapy.

Regarding diabetes, patient reports getting through Halloween okay but did not stick to diet during Thanksgiving week. He is now trying to monitor his intake more carefully. He is still taking metformin.

Regarding hypertension, patient purchased the blood pressure cuff as recommended. Readings have been pretty moderate with nothing out of the ordinary. He is still taking lisinopril with no problems.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, blood in stool, or weight loss.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Type 2 diabetes
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin
Lisinopril

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient enjoys outdoor activities including walking and yard work. Planning vacation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure good in office.
Neck: No carotid bruits appreciated.
Heart: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at left base, previously noted.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Extremities: 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally in lower extremities.

RESULTS
EKG: No concerning findings. Normal for age with risk factors present.
Hemoglobin A1c: 8 (elevated; goal closer to 6).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Refer to psychiatry for talk therapy/counseling, not for medication at this time.
2. Type 2 diabetes: Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Order hemoglobin A1c in couple months. Order lipid panel.
3. Hypertension: Order echocardiogram to recheck heart murmur. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily.
